subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw support a versioned external agent-runtime protocol for non-Node and embedded ports, or remain a hosted JavaScript runtime while independent ports define their own compatibility layer?
rationale: The request adds a broad public architecture and compatibility commitment spanning sessions, tools, streaming, provider/auth behavior, persistence, and security; source evidence does not identify an existing approved protocol boundary that automation can safely implement.

options.title: Sponsor a portable runtime protocol
options.body: Define a narrow, versioned external contract and conformance plan before accepting implementation work for embedded or non-Node runtimes.

options.title: Keep runtime hosting out of scope
options.body: Retain OpenClaw as a JavaScript-hosted product and welcome independent ports only without a supported compatibility ABI.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a portable runtime protocol
recommendation.body: Define a narrow, versioned external contract and conformance plan before accepting implementation work for embedded or non-Node runtimes.

likelyOwner.reason: The current agent-runtime refactor history and existing discussion connect this person most directly to the affected architecture boundary.
